data.exact_reserve_text: In arriving at our reserving position for this loss, the financial implications of multiple scenarios have been modelled, taking account of the uncertainties listed above and utilising a probabilistic framework. In arriving at our reserving position, the likelihood of these scenarios occurring was established using current expert judgement. This reserving approach is consistent with that taken for the year ended 31 December 2022 and reflects updates affecting expert judgment in the year since. This has resulted in ultimate gross reserves of GBP 264.5m (31 December 2022 - GBP 138.3m), GBP 84.5m (31 December 2022 - GBP 39.2m) net of reinsurance. The two classes impacted are Aviation Reinsurance and Aviation War. The loss reserve is split 95% to the 2021 YOA and 5% to the 2022 YOA.
specific_events: Russian invasion of Ukraine / western leased aircraft in Russia
UK building cladding issues (post-Grenfell related PI exposures)

prior_year_events.event_name: Western leased aircraft losses in Russia (Russia/Ukraine exposures)
prior_year_events.impact_description: Significant adverse development on aviation-related exposures driven by the fate of western-leased aircraft in Russia; modelled under multiple scenarios and probabilities updated leading to a large increase in ultimate gross reserves.

Ongoing adverse development on Florida-based contractors book leading to additional IBNR booked during 2023 (additional IBNR GBP 13.2m in the year), contributing to prior-year reserve deterioration across 2014-2019 years of account.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Provision for potential claims relating to building cladding issues; IBNR of GBP 9.7m booked in 2023 to cover further development of this issue (professional indemnity exposures for architects/design-build firms).

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate strengthened gross claims reserves materially in 2023, driven primarily by large geopolitical-related aviation losses arising from the Russian invasion of Ukraine (notably westernleased aircraft in Russia, modelled under multiple scenarios and allocated largely to the 2021 year of account), together with prioryear deterioration in Casualty (notably Florida construction defect litigation) and new IBNR for UK cladding exposures. Inflationary considerations and IBNR recalibration also contributed. The net prioryear strengthening derived from the claims development table is approximately GBP 153.2m (13.1% of opening gross claims outstanding).
raw_causal_phrases: increased reserves for the syndicates indirect Russia/Ukraine losses and prior year deterioration for the Casualty business group.
This has resulted in ultimate gross reserves of GBP 264.5m (31 December 2022 - GBP 138.3m), GBP 84.5m (31 December 2022 - GBP 39.2m) net of reinsurance.

The Casualty business group experienced deterioration to the prior year reserves as a result of construction defect claims in Florida and potential claims arising from building cladding issues in the UK.
additional IBNR of GBP 13.2m was booked in the year bringing the overall reserves for this issue to GBP 79.4m.
IBNR of GBP 9.7m has been booked in 2023 to cover this issue.
The inflation allowance takes account of the expected levels and duration of heightened inflation across the different classes of business and territories where we write business.

Due to the nature of the circumstances mentioned above, the potential for variation to the booked reserves is considerably greater than the normal level of reserve sensitivity to downside risk and the actual outcome of the loss could be in a particularly wide range with greater than usual variability.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prioryear development (PYD) was calculated from the gross claims development (triangle) provided in the accounts (note 14). The report also includes large event-specific reserve movements (notably Russia/Ukraine aircraft) and RITC items in the underwriting-year accounts which can distort aggregate movements; the triangle was used as the primary gross source. Some quantified amounts quoted in the narrative are net of reinsurance or presented in USD in the Underwriter's Report; where gross GBP amounts were not explicitly stated the related figures are left null. Confidence values reflect those considerations.
